fields.h1: Build a Vendor Application for Your Market or Event
fields.hero_description: Get a vendor application that reads insurance dates off each certificate and saves every vendor to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Application Checks Before You Do
fields.features_subheading: What Emergent builds into a vendor application, and what you keep when the season ends.
fields.feature_1:
An application drafted from your event

Describe your market and what you screen vendors for. Emergent builds the application and the screen your reviewers use to score it. Change any question with a follow-up prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that match each vendor type

Food vendors get the permit and insurance questions, and a jeweler gets a photo upload instead. Each applicant answers only what their category needs, in a form that stays short.
fields.feature_3:
Certificates read into fields

Vendors upload a certificate of insurance or a permit, and the app reads the insured name and policy dates into fields. A date it cannot read with confidence goes to a person.
fields.feature_4:
Scores and notes on the vendor's row

Reviewers score each application and leave notes. Each score sits in a database you own, beside the vendor's answers and uploads. Sort by category to fill the booths you have.
fields.feature_5:
Status emails and a nudge for the manager

Each status change sends its own email: accepted, waitlisted, or missing a document. Vendors missing a file get reminders, and the manager gets a Slack alert when a decision is due.
fields.feature_6:
Your web address, your code

Run the application at your event's own web address; custom domains are included and use credits. Paid plans add full code export to your GitHub repository, yours after the season.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Organizers Screen Their Vendors
fields.tab_content_1:
Honey from next door waits for the manager

Every vendor at a producer-only Saturday market sells what their own farm grows. The application asks each farm for its crops and whether it resells anything. A yes holds the application for the market manager, with the answer quoted in full. Fernhill Acres answered yes: honey from a neighbor's hives.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three jurors, one ranked list of jewelers

Jewelers sent 27 applications for 8 booths at a juried craft fair. Three jurors score each applicant's photos out of 5, and the app ranks the averages. The top 8 are accepted. Saltmarsh Silver took the last booth with a 4.3, and the decision emails went out as 8 accepted and 19 not accepted.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each certificate read for its end date

Food vendors at a July 18 street festival upload a certificate of insurance with the application. The app reads the policy start and end dates off each one. Casa Bruma Tacos sent a certificate whose policy ends June 30. Its application is on hold, and the owner has an email asking for a renewed certificate.
fields.tab_content_4:
One cancellation, one offer, 48 hours to answer

A candle maker cancels booth 22 at a holiday market. The app emails the first candle maker on the waitlist, Juniper Lane Candles, an offer that stays open for 48 hours. An offer that lapses moves to the next name in line. Juniper Lane accepted, and the booth map now shows it in booth 22.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Vendor Application
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a vendor application that asks only what you need to pick vendors, then sends each decision.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Set the rules before the fields
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the business basics first
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask what they sell, with photos
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the booth count per category and anything that rules an applicant out, such as reselling at a producer-only market. Every question on the form should help you apply one of those rules, and any question that does not can go.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with the business name, then the person and the email address that should get your decision. Ask for a sales tax permit number only if your event requires one, and use the field's help text to say why you need it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for a short product list, a price range, and 3 to 5 photos of the work and of a past booth. Photos let a jury compare applicants side by side, and the price range shows whether a vendor fits the shoppers you draw.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Place uploads after the questions, once a vendor has invested time in the answers. A certificate of insurance is only evidence of coverage in effect when it was issued. Find the policy end date on each one and compare it with your event date.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Turn booth needs into fixed choices
fields.howto_step_5_des: Offer booth size and power as fixed choices, never free text, and add a corner checkbox if you charge extra for corners. These answers drive the booth map, and a 10x10 with power is far easier to place than a paragraph.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with two fake vendors
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit one application that should pass and one that should be held, such as a certificate that ends before the event. Check that each lands on its own row with the right status, and that each fake vendor gets the email it should.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Post the link on your event's site with a firm deadline. When reviews are done, send every decision email from the same table, and keep this season's rows so next year's invitations go to vendors you already know.

faq_plan.a: A vendor application is the form a business fills out to ask for a spot at a market or festival. It asks what the business sells and how much space it needs, and it collects documents such as a certificate of insurance. The organizer then weighs each one against the booths left in that category.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a vendor application?
faq_plan.ref: how to create a vendor application
faq_plan.a: Describe your event in a prompt: the categories, the booth count, the documents you need, and who reviews. Emergent's AI form builder writes the questions and the status emails to match. Publish it, then email the link to past vendors or print it as a QR code on your flyers.

faq_plan.q: Can you provide an example of a vendor application?
faq_plan.ref: Can you provide an example of a vendor application?

prov.original: Can you provide an example of a vendor application?

faq_plan.a: Yes. A craft fair vendor application might ask for the business name and contact, a product category, a price range, and 4 photos of the work. It then asks for the booth size, whether power is needed, a certificate of insurance, and a signature agreeing to the fair's rules. Emergent can build that form from one prompt, with each category seeing only its own questions.

faq_plan.q: Where do I submit a vendor application form?
faq_plan.ref: where do i submit the atd vendor application form
faq_plan.a: Submit it to whoever runs the event, through the link or address on their call for vendors. Treat a vendor application form like a job application form: send it before the deadline and keep the confirmation email until you hear back. Check whether the booth fee is due now or on acceptance before you pay.

faq_plan.q: What goes on a vendor registration form?
faq_plan.a: Put the vendor's legal name and remittance address on it, plus a Form W-9. The W-9 gives the buyer the vendor's correct taxpayer ID for the information return the buyer files with the IRS. Emergent can build a vendor registration form that collects W-9s and keeps payment records ready for 1099 reporting.

It means a seller's request to be approved before selling: the vendor is the business, and the application is how it asks. Event organizers use the phrase for booth spots, and it also covers selling to a government. Douglas County, Georgia's online vendor application, for one, tells applicants to download the vendor packet and fill out the W-9 form.

faq_plan.q: When should a vendor application open and close?
flagged: PA6 asker unclear: fragment or name (no question word)
faq_plan.a: Open it about four months before the event and close it six weeks out. Those six weeks give your jurors time to score, and give accepted vendors time to send a certificate of insurance before load-in. Put the closing date at the top of the form, and decide now whether a late application goes to the waitlist or gets turned away.

faq_plan.q: What should a vendor application say about cancellations?
flagged: PA6 asker unclear: fragment or name (no question word)
faq_plan.a: It should state the cancellation deadline and what a vendor gets back on each side of it, right above the signature line. A rule such as a full refund up to 30 days out and none after that settles a last-week dropout without a debate. Add a required checkbox agreeing to the policy, and keep the date each vendor checked it with their application.

faq_plan.q: Where do I get a DE vendor application?
flagged: PA6 asker unclear: fragment or name (no question word)
faq_plan.a: If DE means Delaware, apply to whoever runs the sale you want to join, such as the town for a street fair or the fair board for a county fair. Ask for this year's packet, and check the deadline and the insurance limits before you pay the fee. If you run the event, Emergent can build that packet as one online application with no cap on submissions.

faq_plan.q: How do I fill out a vintage markets vendor application?
faq_plan.ref: how to apply vintage markets vendor application
faq_plan.a: Find the market's call for vendors on its website or social pages, and apply on its own form before the deadline. Have photos of your booth and your best pieces ready, and note the eras you carry. Check that the link is the vendor application, not the shopper ticket or registration form for the same market.

plan.angle: The top 10 is county and city vendor portals (LA County, Douglas County, Westfield, Shreveport, Albuquerque) plus market pages (Tampa Bay Markets, Makrs, Market Square) and one Jotform template gallery.
